title: REDUCED FLASHING TONES DOWN THE SITE GOING UP
why: Found in the cloud hunt of 2026-10-15: REDUCED FLASHING says it tones down the bright flashes, but when the clock ran out the site going up still drew its full-screen white-out at full strength and its rapid barrage of blooms at full size and length, because those blooms are pushed straight in and never go through flash(). Proven in headless Chromium with REDUCED FLASHING on: white-out alpha 0.92 (off 0.92) and bloom life 0.5 (off 0.5). With it on, the white-out now takes the same 0.45 factor as the lightning, and the blooms the same smaller and shorter light flash() gives every other blast. With it off nothing changes.
now: REDUCED FLASHING now also tones down the white-out when the site goes up.

edits.replacement: wc.fillStyle='rgba(255,236,196,'+clamp(_nf*flashK(),0,0.94).toFixed(3)+')';   // v16.xx (cloud-menus-nuke-reduced-flash), CLOUD HUNT 2026-10-15: REDUCED FLASHING left this full-screen white-out at full strength; it now takes flashK like the lightning

G.flashes.push({x:bx,y:by,r:rnd(180,340)*(CFG.flashRed===1?0.6:1),t:0,life:0.5*(CFG.flashRed===1?0.7:1),c:'#ffd6a0'});   // v16.xx (cloud-menus-nuke-reduced-flash), CLOUD HUNT 2026-10-15: these blooms skip flash(), so REDUCED FLASHING never shrank them; same factors as flash(), same rnd draw
